required_denominator: annual Boeing family/cohort departures or sectors for 2010-2025 under a compatible global commercial-jet scope, with source-vintage/revision semantics sufficient for reproducible historical baseline construction

sources.source_title: Annual Safety Report sector data + World Air Transport Statistics (WATS)
sources.observed_granularity: public model-level global annual sectors in historical Annex 4 editions through 2019; later public Safety Reports expose aggregate jet/turboprop and regional sectors; current WATS product advertises longitudinal aircraft/model utilization
sources.reason: The 2019 Safety Report Annex 4 publicly provides annual sectors by manufacturer/model for 2015-2019, continuing overlapping public Annex 4 windows back to at least 2010. In the inspected 2021 public report, the sector table is instead jet/turboprop by region rather than manufacturer/model, and the 2023 public material exposes aggregate sector/rate information rather than the former model matrix. A public reproducible manufacturer/model bridge for 2020-2023 has not been demonstrated. IATA currently advertises WATS Global with 2010-2025 historical data and aircraft/model utilization, but WATS is a subscription/proprietary data product rather than a public evidence table. Public 2024-2025 WATS releases expose Boeing 737 all-variant flight frequencies only. Historical Safety Report sector figures are revision-sensitive and IATA states that historical values may differ across editions as sector data are updated.

sources.source_title: Statistical Summary of Commercial Jet Airplane Accidents
sources.observed_granularity: annual worldwide all-commercial-jet departures/flight-hours plus cumulative Boeing/type statistics
sources.reason: No complete annual Boeing-family departures/cycles matrix for the required 2010-2025 cohort-year cells has been demonstrated. Aggregate fleet totals and cumulative type rates cannot be inverted or disaggregated into family-year exposure.

sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Transportation / Bureau of Transportation Statistics
sources.observed_granularity: monthly non-stop segment records by aircraft type/service class with scheduled/performed departures and aircraft hours
sources.reason: The database covers U.S. domestic operations and international operations with at least one U.S./territory service point; foreign-to-foreign flights are excluded. It can support sensitivity/reconciliation work but cannot serve as the global BSFM family-year denominator.

sources.source_title: ICAO Long Term Traffic Forecast application
sources.observed_granularity: historical traffic by carrier/country-pair/route-group/region plus forecasts of departures and fleet forecasts by aircraft type
sources.reason: The public product description does not establish a reproducible historical actual-departures matrix at Boeing-family-by-year granularity matching the BSFM denominator. Forecasted departures/fleet are not substitutes for historical measured exposure, and no new paid ICAO API dependency is permitted.

vintage_policy_requirement.reason: IATA states that Safety Report sector figures use the most up-to-date data available at report production and that historical figures can change as sources and classifications are updated. Any historical baseline therefore needs an explicit rule choosing contemporaneous report vintages or a versioned modern reconstruction; the two must not be mixed silently.

prohibited_transformations: allocate aggregate departures to Boeing families using fleet share
split Boeing 737 all-variant sectors into Original/Classic/NG/MAX using fleet share, deliveries, market share or accident counts
invert cumulative accident rates to reconstruct annual family departures
use fleet counts, deliveries, capacity or market share as the primary denominator
substitute forecast departures for historical measured departures
mix revised modern historical sector values with contemporaneous-vintage values without a declared version policy

conclusion.next_research_direction: Do not treat the 2020-2023 gap as a simple missing-download problem. Determine whether a reproducible/licensable WATS extraction or another global model-level source can legally and methodologically populate all required historical cohort-year cells, including 727 and 737 Original/Classic/NG/MAX, with a declared vintage rule. If not, retain G2 BLOCKED or prospectively version a different cohort design without rewriting the frozen F-002 target/evaluation.
